one_month_reasoning: Two dated events, both late in the window. (1) GEV Q3 2026 results on 2026-10-28 before the open [14], the same day as the FOMC decision (Oct 27-28), which follows the first hike since 2023 on 9/16 to 3.75-4.00% with another hike signalled [44]. Orders are pre-signalled as very strong [22,42], but per the Laguna transcript most of the new slot and contract adds land in 4Q rather than 3Q, and Electrification data-center orders fall as a share of the segment [45]; EPS after a 2Q miss is the swing factor. So the orders upside is partly pre-announced and partly deferred, and the stock has already bounced ~13% from the $874.76 close on 9/14. (2) Hyperscaler Q3 results in the last week of October: the chain read is supportive (no capex cuts after the 9/12-14 AI-slowdown calls; Oracle guided ~$70B FY27 outlay with RPO $664B; Goldman sees 2027 hyperscaler capex up ~54%) [17,46,47], so a capex cut is a tail, not the base. Oct 31 is a Saturday, so the 10/30 close counts. Net: I drop most of my round-1 positive tilt: median ~$992 (+0.5%), log-sd ~16% (52%/3.5 plus an earnings-and-FOMC-day premium), near-symmetric.

fair_value.method: Blend of 50% P/E (2028E EPS $31.2 x 31x = $967), 30% FCF yield (normalized FCF $8.0B / 3.2% / 263M shares = $951) and 20% EV/EBITDA (2028E EBITDA $11.5B x 21x + $10.5B net cash, over 263M shares = $958). Fair value about $960 for Oct 2027, about 3% below spot; lower than round 1 ($1,040) because 2028 revenue is now anchored between guidance ($56B) and consensus ($61.3B), the FCF floor is >= $24B for 2025-28 (implying >= ~$8.3B across 2027-28), and multiples are trimmed for the 9/16 Fed hike.

bear.story: AI-capex digestion: 2027-28 hyperscaler plans get cut or slip (capex already ~100% of cloud revenue, more external financing), behind-the-meter projects are cancelled (Crusoe-Boom template), Texas's audit holds back ~50 GW of load and slot reservations (63 of 116 GW) convert slowly. Siemens, MHI, Doosan and Baker Hughes capacity arrives into GLJ's 2030-31 glut, and higher rates compress the multiple. ~21-22x on ~$28 2028E EPS.

base.story: Gas reaches >125 GW under contract by YE26, the $200B backlog arrives early 2027, the January 2027 call shows margin in backlog rising and the spring-2027 CMD sets a 2030 outlook that rerates out-year earnings; Electrification grows 20%+ on transformer shortages and a 307 GW US data-center backlog (Eaton). 2028E EPS ~$31-32 at ~33-34x near the CMD.

bull.story: Hyperscaler capex reaches $1.2-1.3T in 2027 (Goldman, S&P Global) without the 2028 slowdown, PJM shortfalls and grid limits push more utility and behind-the-meter gas orders, $/kW keeps rising and the CMD lifts 2028 beyond consensus revenue: EPS ~$36 at ~41x.

thesis_break_reason: Below about $640 (35% under today, ~20.5x a ~$31 2028E EPS, the multiple of a no-premium peer such as Siemens Energy), the market would be pricing a real drop in gas order intake, slot reservations failing to convert, margin in backlog stalling at the January 2027 disclosure, or a structural hyperscaler capex cut, not ordinary 50%-vol noise. Any of these breaks the sold-out-through-2030 story that Siemens Energy, MHI and GEV all tell. Unchanged from round 1; the corrections lower my fair value but do not change what a fundamental break looks like.

reasoning: Round 2, industry lane, 8 additional searches/fetches. The supervisor corrected three things I accept: the 2025-28 FCF floor is >= $24B (4Q25 release [43]), set when 2026 was guided at $5.0-5.5B, so the 2026 raise to ~$12B pulls cash forward and implies >= ~$8.3B over 2027-28; net cash is a verified $10.3B (10-Q [15]); and the FOMC hiked to 3.75-4.00% on 9/16 with more priced [44], which I had not reflected. I also accept the catalyst calendar (January call, spring CMD [45]). On the supervisor's suggestion to haircut 2028 revenue toward $56B, I go halfway ($59B): the January outlook predates the 2026 order and pricing step-up the chain documents (Siemens 15 GW quarter and 110-120 GW/yr market view [49,41], GEV orders doubling [2]), so I do not move fully to guidance. Chain checks since round 1 are neutral to mildly positive: no hyperscaler capex cuts after the AI-slowdown calls, Goldman sees ~$1.2T 2027 capex but growth slowing to ~12% in 2028 [46], Oracle guides ~$70B FY27 outlay with RPO $664B [47], and trade press still describes multi-year turbine waits [48]. The 2028 deceleration matters for the multiple paid in Oct 2027. Revaluation: P/E $967, FCF yield $951, EV/EBITDA $958, blended ~$960 (down from $1,040), ~3% below spot. Distribution: mixture of a base lognormal (median $1,075, sigma 0.38, weight 0.80, reflecting the January call and spring CMD as rerating events in the horizon and a median analyst target of ~$1,250 as evidence of upside skew) and a 20% bear component (median $640, sigma 0.32). P(>=987) falls from 0.52 to 0.49; mean ~$1,050. Thesis break stays $640.
